result:
**No.**

Counterexample: take [a,b] = [0,1] and let f be Thomae's function, with f(p/q) = 1/q for p/q in lowest terms and f(x) = 0 for irrational x.

1. f is Riemann integrable, since it is bounded and continuous except on the rationals, a null set.
2. Every subinterval contains an irrational point, where f = 0, so every lower Darboux sum satisfies L(f,P) = 0 for every partition P.
3. Every subinterval also contains a rational point, where f > 0, so f is not constant on any open subinterval.
4. Since f ≥ 0 and f = 0 at every irrational, 0 = L(f,P) ≤ ∫f ≤ U(f,P). Refining P makes U(f,P) arbitrarily small (the set {f ≥ ε} is finite for each ε > 0), so ∫₀¹ f = 0.
5. Hence L(f,P_n) = 0 = ∫f for every sequence of partitions P_n, so the hypothesis holds.
6. Take P_n = {0,1} for all n. Then λ(P_n) = 1, which does not tend to 0.

The hypothesis "for any sequence" is in fact very strong. Applied to the trivial partitions, it forces (inf f)(b−a) = ∫f, meaning f = inf f almost everywhere, so f is far from generic. The "not constant on any open subinterval" condition does not rule this out, as the example shows. The same example also defeats the weaker reading "for some sequence P_n".

Final answer: No
